ADVISOR INVENTORY DISPOSITION / C DESIGN BINDINGS — STORY-1843, codex2 writer/retirement held-lock inventory at main3cbb90b0c94e (/tmp/codex2-story1843-writer-retirement-lock-inventory.txt). Accepted as a concrete entry/callchain assessment with explicit gaps, NOT as implemented fencing or a proof of a globally acyclic graph. Advisor independently checked Pool::with_state_lock, teardown_worktree_path, store_push_pull publication and session_end's warn-and-clean-up behavior against the stated ordering.
1. Pool/retirement choice: use durable staged retiring/reserved state. The Pool-owned phase may take Lifecycle in Pool→Lifecycle order, but do not hold either new lifecycle/receipt locks across arbitrary hooks, network/model work, or long Git operations. A safe implementation must reserve/fence the source under the actual outer pool scope, establish quiescence and preservation, release locks for external work, then revalidate exact generation/identity and finalize under the prescribed order. Generic post-remove pool deregistration occurs after Lifecycle release. No held helper reacquires Pool. A hook string is not writer capability: unknown/in-flight/legacy mutators cannot be assumed quiescent; refusal keeps recovery state. Opaque hook/partial-failure cases need deterministic tests; do not just move the deadlock to another phase.
2. Canonical publication choice: pre-admit the exact intentional source-local publication BEFORE Store; carry a typed, generation-bound admitted-operation permit through the existing Store-held closure, with a real lifetime/quiescence rule. The permit must keep retirement from winning while its admitted writer can still publish; it cannot be an unchecked boolean, filename, raw env token or path-only snapshot. Do not acquire Lifecycle opportunistically from Store-held digest and do not hold Lifecycle across push/pull network/hooks. The doer's concrete permit/failure/recovery plan must show how admission is released and how crashed/unknown/in-flight descendants remain fenced; PID death alone is not proof every writer is gone. Existing store recursion and Store→Dispense order remain. No new public digest/sync is a private-retention substitute.
3. Add an explicit canonical-mutation coverage check to C/STORY1742 ownership: store Git intake/rebase/union/fast-forward/checkout can change canonical mailbox files even when it does not call write_message_in. Account for those paths and canonical remove_store_worktree, rather than claiming explicit JSON writers exhaust canonical mutations. Coordinate the already-signed shared-writer owner/protocol, preserve transport-policy preflight before persistent publication, and do not move a public mailbox publication earlier merely to avoid a lock. Read-only B query scaffolding is not blocked on inventing another writer, but B ACK/C activation is not complete until these admitted lifetimes are proven.
4. Clone anchor choice: use an EXPLICIT verified host-recorded clone→main/common-Git binding (existing host_recorded_clone/main_for evidence, pinned and validated in its proper owner) to retain privately OUTSIDE the directory to be deleted. The clone's own common dir dies with remove_dir_all and cannot be its durable retention home. An unverified/missing/stale host binding refuses destruction and retains the tree/recovery evidence; never guess main from neighbor/origin/store parent, sweep unrelated clones, or run prohibited host Git inside the clone. B's ordinary same-common inventory remains narrow; C's verified retained-source manifest admits the intentional clone source.
5. Failed preservation/removal must not flow through today's warn-then-release ownership cleanup. Keep source, exact lease/claim/pin/manifest recovery association until the operation is known safe, and make refusal observable/non-success. This does NOT authorize resurrecting an already revoked grant or delaying a security revocation the caller requires. Represent ending/revoked-but-retained recovery truthfully; do not label it active authority or completed cleanup. Preserve original token/identity compare-delete guarantees. Reuse/reset must quarantine/preserve ignored old mail before a new occupant is admitted.
6. Receipt/authority choice: resolve facts before locks; under Lifecycle→Receipt use ONLY protected read-only validation of the same subject/parent/roster/native binding/source versions. No occupancy authorize/SeatPermit acquisition, namespace touch/reserve, grant mutation, Store acquisition, callback dispatch or recursive lifecycle admission under Receipt. Changed evidence drops locks and boundedly retries/refuses. Do not claim stronger revocation linearization than the actual checked observation; do not add a new grant requirement to mail paths that currently do not need one. Existing outer Seat/tick/disk scopes stay explicit and cannot be reacquired by a helper.
7. C3 is still operator-run and fail-closed on unknown/mixed writer capability. Include actual old REST/MCP/core hosts, transient CLI/scheduler/hook and in-flight writers, not just CLI version labels or a successful atomic copy/upgrade. Layout barriers/open-FD checks alone do not prove no late writer can recreate a removed path. No live install/migration/activation/revocation/cleanup authorized by this design assessment. Existing local-only/non-Git API callers also need an explicit compatibility/coverage decision before imposing a new Git requirement; they must not borrow another repository's anchor or be silently advertised globally complete.
8. The reader inventory prerequisite is now concrete enough for the already-approved A preparation and then B1 read-only/context/conformance work, with retention coverage explicitly unestablished until C. B2 shared ACK and C source lifecycle must be integrated in their real supported ordering; do not expose a success-shaped stub or deploy a binary whose ordinary ACK has no real compatible lifecycle provider. Full B/C/D/E, TASK2345/46 and relay STORY122 remain mandatory. A helper/slice is non-completing Refs only. Complete the exact canonical-permit and mixed-mutator/clone failure fixtures in the implementation plan and independent STRICT review before claiming those guarantees. No full parent completion, scope reduction or permission/role change is implied.
subject: STORY1843 inventory accepted; C ordering/clone/recovery decisions pinned
